title: Mitigate TPU Hardware Fault
description: Restart the TPU workload once (only after the previous attempt's pods are gone) to test for a transient fault. If the same TPU worker shows up as an outlier repeatedly, capture the host information and request Google to isolate the bad host.
instruction:
Mitigate a suspected TPU hardware fault on host `${host_name}`:
1. Precondition for any restart: the previous attempt has 0 pods left (`kubectl get pods -n <ns> | grep <workload>` returns nothing, including Terminating pods) and no `FailedKillPod` events (`kubectl get events -n <ns> --field-selector reason=FailedKillPod`). If pods are stuck Terminating, do NOT restart or resubmit: a new slice can be formed on TPUs still held by the old containers and take down many hosts at once. Follow [[kueue-stuck-termination-recovery]] and [[gotchas-kubernetes-gke]] instead. Once the precondition holds, ask the workload owner (this action restarts nothing itself) to restart once to verify whether the hang/interruption is transient.
2. If it fails again, analyze the coordinator logs to locate outlier TPU workers, and confirm whether `${host_name}` is among them.
3. Verify whether `${host_name}` repeatedly shows up as the outlier. Count distinct *incidents*, not raw log lines: a single host death is reported by every surviving peer at once, so event counts inflate one failure into dozens.
4. If it is a repeat offender, extract its GCE host/node mapping and isolate it. For GKE-managed TPUs use [[isolate-node-via-rr-label]] via [[node-isolation-and-rr-api]]; isolate-node-via-rr-label is cluster-only and does not apply to a GKE node.

host_name.description: The suspected culprit host, quoted from logs rather than inferred from device coordinates.
